corrections.source_says: The paper reports two groups but never states how participants were allocated; Figure 1 also gives no allocation method. Under form-spec.md, quasi_people requires nonrandom assignment, which is not established by an unreported method. Use other with the description 'two-group comparative experiment; assignment not stated', retain assignment.randomized='not_stated', and revise the corresponding explanation in eligibility.reason. There is no evidence supporting an RCT classification either.
corrections.quote: The experiment is divided into a traditional search engine group (using Pinterest, n = 6) and an AIGC group (using Midjourney, n = 6).
corrections.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 105), Method and Figure 1; form-spec.md, Field notes, design_class definition

confirmed: Read the complete markdown and all 11 PDF pages, including references; visually checked Figures 1-3. The document is the published AHFE Open Access paper in Creativity, Innovation and Entrepreneurship, Vol. 166 (2025), pp. 103-113, DOI 10.54941/ahfe1006116; its title and authors match the form (PDF p. 1, printed p. 103).

The sample is 12 design master's students: 7 females, 5 males, average age 23, with 4-5 years of design learning experience; each tool group has 6 participants. No exclusions or separate randomized and analyzed totals are reported; the participant sample is below 50 (PDF p. 3, printed p. 105, Method).

Pinterest and Midjourney are the two inspiration sources, and both groups perform low- and high-constraint brainstorming tasks. Neither the text nor the procedure figure reports random assignment; n_randomized=null and assignment.randomized=not_stated are supported (PDF p. 3, printed p. 105, Method and Figure 1).

Figure 1 shows a 5-minute introduction, a 20-minute low-constraint task, a 5-minute review, a 20-minute high-constraint task, another 5-minute review, and a 15-20-minute interview. The text instead reports interviews averaging 20-30 minutes, as the form explicitly notes (PDF p. 3, printed p. 105, Method and Figure 1).

The Mars-survival task is supported by the participant quotation and Figure 2; car interior/cabin sleep design is supported by Table 1 and Figure 3. The form identifies the latter description as derived from keywords (PDF pp. 4-5, printed pp. 106-107).

S1-O1 reported is exact: traditional-search users selected 241 inspiration-related images and AIGC users selected 76. These are image counts, not people or participant-produced design scores, and no inferential test accompanies this contrast (PDF p. 6, printed p. 108, Inspiration Selection Phase).

S1-O2 reported matches the text: low-constraint AIGC use showed no significant commonality in extended subject words, while technology and minimalism were shared style terms absent from traditional-search keywords; high-constraint AIGC use showed no commonality in extended style words. Figures 2-3 show search-input words, with no numerical commonality statistic or inferential test (PDF pp. 4-5, printed pp. 106-107, Design Definition Phase and Figures 2-3).

The one-line finding is supported: the participant count and image counts are correct, and deeper iterative AIGC search is a qualitative observation rather than a scored creativity effect (PDF p. 3, printed p. 105, Method; PDF pp. 6-7, printed pp. 108-109, Inspiration Search Phase and Table 3).

No creativity or diversity measure is scored on participant-produced design output. Results concern search keywords, search behavior, selected inspiration images, and think-aloud/interview observations; core=no, criterion_2=not_met, criterion_3=not_met, and context_class=none are supported. No randomized people study with a qualifying scored output is established (PDF pp. 2-9, printed pp. 104-111, Method, Results, and Conclusion).

This is one original comparative study, not a synthesis; the empty synthesis fields are appropriate. No supplementary material, appendix, preregistration, data/code link, or shared-sample claim is stated; acknowledgment names Hunan University and its Digital Intelligence and Cultural Innovation Laboratory, with no company involvement reported (entire PDF, especially PDF p. 10, printed p. 112, Acknowledgment).
summary: The paper confirms 12 participants, image counts of 76 versus 241, and no scored creativity or diversity outcome. One correction is needed: assignment is unspecified, so quasi_people asserts more than the source supports.
